newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-LONG KEEPS CALM AS DALY CRASHES OUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LONG KEEPS CALM AS DALY CRASHES OUT.

text.p: New Zealander Michael Long took a two-shot lead in the opening tournament on the European PGA Tour after the second round on Friday as American John Daly missed the cut by a massive 10 shots.

Long shot a second successive 68 for an eight-under par aggregate of 136 to move clear of South African Ernie Els and Australia's Peter Lonard at the half-way stage of the 700,000 pounds sterling (US$1.1 million) Johnnie Walker Classic, an event jointly sanctioned by the Australian PGA Tour.
But there was embarrassment for Daly, the former British Open and U.S. PGA champion, who failed to live up to his billing as a major drawcard with a dismal seven over par 79 to add to his opening 77.
Frenchan Jean Van de Velde and England's Paul Eales shared third place on five under par at the Hope Island resort course.

Long, winner of last year's New Zealand Open, enjoyed the early calm and finished strongly with an eagle and birdie on the last two holes before the increasingly blustery conditions sent scores spiralling during the afternoon.
"I'm playing better each day. There was a bad patch in the middle and then suddenly it all turned around," Long, 28, said.
"Maybe in the past I wanted every shot to be perfect and a bad patch affected me too much. I'm learning how to stay positive and not get angry. After five years on tour it's beginning to sink in."
Els said the increasingly blustery conditions gave players who went out early, like himself, a one or two shot advantage over those teeing off later in the day.
"On the second nine, the wind really started to get up. It's nice to play in the mornings," said Els, who added a 68, including an eagle and three birdies, to his opening 70.
"I'm hitting the ball reasonably well and the way I'm playing at the moment I'm about 80 percent of the way to being where I want to be with my game."

Of the other pre-tournament favourites, Englishman Nick Faldo stayed in contention, six shots behind Long on two under, with a par 72. Defending champion Ian Woosnam of Wales was a further two shots back on level par.

Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, seeking to capture his fifth successive European Order of Merit in a row, slipped down the field with a second round 74 to finish one over and survive the cut by a single stroke.
